# PhysicsFingers

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Interaction.Runtime` · assembly `VRFramework.Interaction.Runtime` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/interaction/physics-hold/Runtime/Scripts/Interaction/PhysicsFingers.cs#L26)

Gives a hand's fingers bodies of their own, so they can push things about, be stopped by the
world, and hold the hand off whatever they land on.

The middle layer of the three-layer hand, applied past the wrist. One small capsule body per
fingertip, driven by the same clamped velocity controller as the palm, colliding only with
the layers the scene's [`PokeInteractable`](/api/vrframework-interaction-runtime/PokeInteractable) surfaces sit on.

Nothing deforms the drawn finger. It keeps the shape the player's own hand is making, and
what keeps it out of a wall is the wall stopping the *hand*: a finger pressing on
something presses back on the arm just as hard, and that reaction goes to the palm body.
See [`reaction`](/api/vrframework-interaction-runtime/PhysicsFingers#reaction), which is off by default.

Nothing happens while the hand is holding something. A held object owns the fingers, and its
own grip already decides where they are.

```csharp
[DefaultExecutionOrder(-100)]
public class PhysicsFingers : MonoBehaviour
```

## Fields

### brace {#brace}

How much of the arm's push one braced fingertip can hold, in newtons. Separate from
[`strength`](/api/vrframework-interaction-runtime/PhysicsFingers#strength) and much larger: pushing a ball is done with the finger, holding a
hand off a table is done with the arm. Raise it if fingers still go through what they land on.

### fingerMass {#fingermass}

How heavy one finger is, in kilograms. Decides how much it is thrown about by what it hits,

### letGo {#letgo}

Ceiling on how long a released object goes on being ignored by the fingers, in seconds. The
fingers are wrapped around whatever is held, so they are inside it at the moment of letting
go; the exemption comes back as soon as they are clear.

```csharp
[Tooltip("How long a released object goes on being ignored by the fingers, in seconds.\n\nThe fingers are wrapped around whatever is held, so they are inside it at the moment of letting go, and restoring the collision there and then throws it. The exemption comes back as soon as they are clear of each other; this is only the ceiling on waiting for that.")]
[Range(0, 2)]
```

### reaction {#reaction}

How much of what a finger leans on is leaned back on the hand, 0 to 1. Off by default: at 0
the fingers are stopped and the hand is not, which is what poking, pressing and buttons all
use. At 1 the hand is held off whatever its fingertips found, which needs a
[`PhysicsHand`](/api/vrframework-interaction-runtime/PhysicsHand) to reach anything.

```csharp
[Tooltip("How much of what a finger leans on is leaned back on the hand, 0 to 1.\n\nAt 0 the fingers are stopped by what they land on and the hand is not, so the drawn fingers carry on into whatever stopped them. Poking, pressing and buttons all work at 0, which is the default.\n\nAt 1 the hand itself is held off whatever its fingertips found. Try it per scene rather than as a rule; it is the part of this that behaves differently on a head than in a measurement.\n\nThe hand needs a Physics Hand for this to reach anything.")]
[Range(0, 1)]
public float reaction
```

**Returns** [`float`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.single)

### recover {#recover}

How far a finger may be left behind before it gives up and jumps to the tracked one, in
metres. Only ever applied to a finger resting on nothing, so a braced one is never snapped
through what it is holding the hand off.

### stopsOn {#stopson}

Extra layers a finger may collide on, on top of wherever the scene's poke surfaces are.
Normally nothing: the layers are read off the surfaces themselves, so adding a
[`PokeInteractable`](/api/vrframework-interaction-runtime/PokeInteractable) is all it takes for fingers to meet something.

```csharp
[Tooltip("Extra layers a finger may collide on, on top of wherever the scene's poke surfaces are.\n\nNormally nothing, and it does not need to be anything: the layers are read off the surfaces themselves, so adding a Poke Interactable to something is all it takes for fingers to meet it.")]
public LayerMask stopsOn
```

### Refresh() {#refresh}

```csharp

```

### Release() {#release}

Destroys the bodies and forgets them. Needed outside play mode, where OnDisable never runs
and the bodies of a hand that has been torn down are left in the scene - where the next
hand's fingers collide with them and are pushed about by a hand that no longer exists.

```csharp
public void Release()
```
